text: WASHINGTON One of the most striking things ever said of him is, "that he changed mankind's ideas of political greatness." To commanding talent, and to success, the common ele ments of such greatness, he added a disregard of self, a spotlessness of motive, a steady submission to every public and private duty, which threw far into the shade the whole crowd of vulgar great. The consequence is, that his fame is as durable as his principles, as lasting as truth and virtue themselves.
